desc: Model walk as edge-crossing LP: x_i crossings of edge (i-1,i), total moves = sum x_i, x_i >= 1, parity odd iff end >= i, x_i + x_{i+1} >= 2*v[i] - [end==i]; right-to-left greedy optimal per end e
Discover parity simplification: suffix right of e is even-parity (one precomputed pass); prefix left of e only queried at odd t where x_i(t) = max(1, 2*v[i]-t) exactly (no-parity clamp)
Implement segment tree of composed clamp functions with breakpoint lists + two-pointer merge to answer psum_{e-1}(t) queries in O(log n)

Verify correctness by brute force: BFS/DP enumerator for n ≤ 4, m ≤ 12 over all move sequences; compare vs min_moves and full maxScore on exhaustive + randomized small tests; fix any bugs in compose/evalF/query_prefix (including NEG_INF handling, segment merging, binary search in evalF)
Execute the program on the exhaustive grid (n ≤ 3, values {1..4}, m ≤ 10) and randomized n = 4, m ≤ 12 cases; if any assert fires, debug compose's two-pointer merge (the main residual risk)
If the assert fires, debug compose/evalF against a direct O(n) per-e greedy reference implementation of the edge-crossing LP (simple, obviously correct) and fix the segment-tree logic
Once validated, strip the brute-force/assert branch for the final submission (it is only a testing scaffold) and re-verify examples ([2,4], m=3 → 4; [1,2,3], m=5 → 2)

Stress performance: n = 5·10^4, random points, m = 10^9; confirm breakpoint lists stay small and runtime is acceptable; if the segment tree is too slow in Python, fall back to deriving the O(n) closed-form check
Tighten binary-search upper bound (e.g., best index bound points[i] * floor((m - i + 1)/2) style) to reduce iterations if needed
Edge-case tests: n=2 m=1; m == n (single sweep); all-equal points; points containing 1; m = 1e9; confirm X=3 infeasible for [1,2,3], m=5
